This .NET 10/C# 14 codebase implements **csharparr**, a Transmission RPC-compatible put.io/*arr proxy (Sonarr/Radarr/Whisparr). Stack: ASP.NET Core, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience + Polly, System.CommandLine, Tomlyn, xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions.

Write concise, idiomatic C#; prefer simplicity; keep solutions focused and minimal. Avoid over-engineering—don't add features, abstractions, or "improvements" beyond what's requested. Use OOP with LINQ/pattern matching where appropriate.

Use `Commands/`, `Configuration/`, `Download/`, `Http/`, `Services/`, `Program.cs`, and `tests/Csharparr.Tests/{Configuration,Download,Http,Services,Integration}/`. Follow PascalCase public/types, camelCase locals/parameters, `_camelCase` fields, `I` interfaces. Use file-scoped namespaces, records, nullable references, top-level `Program.cs`, `[]`, `Lock`, primary constructors, raw strings, `var` when obvious, focused methods (~50 lines), and expression-bodied members.

All I/O-bound operations must be async. Always pass `CancellationToken` through the call chain; use `cancellationToken = default` for optional parameters; suffix async methods with `Async`. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log cancellation at Debug, not Error.

Use `BackgroundService`, bounded `Channel<T>`, task tracking, cleanup, typed/named clients, `IHttpClientFactory`, operation-specific timeouts, exponential-backoff+jitter retries and circuit breakers. Retry `HttpRequestException`, `TimeoutException`, `TaskCanceledException`, and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. Use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` (not deprecated `Polly.Extensions.Http`).

Register configuration as singleton: `services.AddSingleton(config)`. Always register services with their interfaces, not concrete types. Use exceptions for exceptional cases; `PutioException`/`ArrClientException`; truncate response bodies to 500 chars. Continue processing other operations when one service fails. Log structured templates, not interpolation; don't log expected conditions at Error.

Use `Lock` type (C# 13+) instead of `lock(object)`; thread-safe collections or locks; periodically clean completed tasks/expired entries.

Tests use xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing`; test happy/error paths and DI via `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`.

Use Tomlyn; validate startup configuration
